title: impact-rule/first-cut 0.1.0-draft
description: Two object families: (1) the parsed rules FILE (TOML, read as an equivalent JSON structure by tomllib — this schema describes that JSON-shaped structure, not TOML syntax itself), and (2) one FIRED ENTRY of `impact_evaluate.py`'s report. SHAPE vs SEMANTICS: this schema is shape/enum-normative for both; a few cross-field/cross-document rules are stated in `x-semantic-only-rules` below because this draft does not encode them structurally — `tools/impact_rules.py` is the executable norm for those. DERIVERS (`derive[]`) have a closed name and typed per-deriver parameter registry (see `deriver_string`/`deriver_table`) but are never evaluated — see the evaluate report's `not_evaluated_derivers`.

closed_decider.description: One of a small closed set of actor-kind tags for decided_by.{detect,fix} below: which kind of actor can notice the need for an update, and which kind is positioned to make it.

urgency.description: One of three closed literals, or the parameterized form 'within:<duration>' where <duration> matches ^[1-9][0-9]*[dhm]$. This schema's `pattern` alternation checks the SHAPE of the parameterized form only; it does not check that the duration has no leading zero beyond what the pattern itself already excludes — `tools/impact_rules.py::_validate_urgency` is the executable norm.

glob_string.description: A when.changed[] entry. Minimal shape check (non-empty string); this draft does not encode the full glob grammar (no absolute path, no '.'/'..' segment, '**' as its own whole segment, allowed character set, an optional '<repo>:' cross-repo prefix whose <repo> is a valid repo id, and the length/segment/'*'-count size limits) — `tools/impact_rules.py::validate_glob_grammar` checks it (see x-semantic-only-rules 'glob-grammar').

when.description: SEMANTIC: exactly one of changed/event is required — a cross-field XOR this draft does not encode; `tools/impact_rules.py::_validate_when` checks it.

decided_by.description: Who can notice the need for this update (`detect`) and who is positioned to make the fix (`fix`) — two closed-vocabulary actor-kind tags.

rule.description: SEMANTIC: `id` must be unique within its file AND across every --rules file passed to one invocation, earlier file wins — a cross-document rule this draft does not encode; `tools/impact_rules.py::validate_merged` checks it. `retrigger` defaults to 'every-event' when absent.

deriver_table.description: A typed registry: the table has exactly one closed deriver-name key. `git-cochange` accepts only optional `min_support` (integer >=1), `min_confidence` (number from 0 through 1), and `advisory` (boolean); the other three derivers accept only an empty params table. Every parameter value must also be JSON-representable, and every integer must fit the signed 64-bit range; `tools/impact_rules.py::_validate_derive_entry`/`_find_non_json_value` enforce those validation-time rules (exit `E_BAD_DERIVE`/18).

rules_file.description: SEMANTIC: `repo` must be a valid <repo> id (`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*$`, 1-64 characters, no control character) — this draft's `minLength` check alone does not encode that charset/length rule; `tools/impact_rules.py::validate_one_doc` checks it.

fired_entry.description: One element of impact_evaluate.py's `fired` array. `obligation` is present only when --obligations was passed — a REPORT-ONLY summary shaped like `obligation_projection` below, not a `format_obligation` duty record.

obligation_projection.description: A REPORT-ONLY SUMMARY of one fired entry, shaped like a small subset of a format_obligation duty record's fields — NOT a format_obligation duty record and not conformant to that format: it carries none of that format's own required identity/provenance/status fields (id, natural_key, scope, source, source_revision, duty_kind, authority, created_by, created_at, occurrences, status, waiver, discharge_evidence, …). A caller that wants a real duty record builds one FROM this summary; this summary is not one and needs no such conversion to be understood as report-only.

required_by.description: An ISO-8601 datetime (for urgency: within:<duration>) or one of the three symbolic literals before-commit/same-session/next-maturity-event.

error_item.description: One diagnostic emitted by an impact-rule tool.

evaluate_report.description: SEMANTIC: status=='unknown' REQUIRES fired==null and not_evaluated_derivers==null (invalid input never reports an empty fired list); status=='ok' REQUIRES both to be arrays (possibly empty). This draft does not encode that conditional; `tools/impact_evaluate.py` enforces it.

run_case_report.description: Closed internal self-test envelope. Every success and error form carries the inner command status and its schema-valid evaluate report.

x-semantic-only-rules.description: Every when.changed[] entry must satisfy the full grammar: an optional '<repo>:' cross-repo prefix (a valid <repo> id), no leading '/', no '.'/'..' segment, no empty segment, '**' only as a whole segment, each other segment restricted to [A-Za-z0-9_.*-]+, no control character, and size limits (<=1024 characters, <=64 segments, <=16 '*' per segment). The schema's glob_string def only requires a non-empty string.
rule.when must carry exactly one of 'changed'/'event' — both or neither is invalid.
A rule id must be unique within one rules file AND across every --rules file passed to one invocation; a later file may not redefine an earlier file's id.
Every <repo> id — the top-level 'repo' field, and any '<repo>:' cross-repo prefix in a glob or a changed path — matches ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*$, 1-64 characters, with no control character.
The 'within:<duration>' duration must be a POSITIVE integer (no '0d', no leading zeros, no fractional units) followed by exactly one of d/h/m.
The evaluate report's fired[] array is sorted by importance rank, then urgency rank (duration-ordered within the 'within' class), then rule_id, then target.
A derive[] entry never contributes a fired[] entry; it only ever appears, once validated, in not_evaluated_derivers.

Every --changed/--changed-file entry must satisfy the same grammar as an authored glob (see glob-grammar above), sized against the larger changed-path size ceiling (<=4096 characters, <=256 segments); a violating entry is reported as an input error, never a crash or a silent non-match.
